To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified a novel gene (D‐PCa 2) highly overexpressed specifically in normal and malignant prostatic tissue and that the corresponding transcripts are detectable by RT‐PCR even in single metastatic cells.
D‐PCa2 is a novel transcript with a highly prostate‐specific pattern of expression and with a potential use as a sensitive marker to detect PCa in lymph nodes.
we have identified a novel prostate specific gene, which may be useful for diagnosis of prostate cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of molecular markers for the diagnosis of prostate cancer (PCa).
the identification of genes selectively expressed or overexpressed in tumors or individual organs.
the discovery and characterization of novel genes selectively expressed in human prostate and/or prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
D‐PCa 2 has the potential to be used as a diagnostic marker for prostate cancer.
D‐PCa2 is a novel gene that is highly expressed in prostate tissue and prostate cancer.
D‐PCa-2 is a highly tissue specific marker for the prostate, and is therefore a useful tool for the diagnosis of PC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a novel transcript that is highly specific to prostate cancer.

we have identified the novel gene PCa‐2, which is highly over‐ expressed in normal prostate tissue, in prostate cancer, in some additional tumors and in the metastatic prostate cancer cell line LNCaP.
we have identified a new gene that is specifically expressed in the prostate.

the expression of the gene D‐PC‐2 is very specific to the prostate and that it is overexpressed in prostate cancer.
the D-PCa-2 gene is highly expressed in prostate and prostate cancer, and it may be useful in the diagnosis of prostate cancer.
